title: Google Health is ending pairing support for older Fitbit scales on November 28
summary: The hardware lives on, but its second chance at syncing won't.
body: TL;DR Google is ending pairing and re-pairing support for Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales on November 28, 2026. Some owners are already unable to connect their scales, despite the official deadline still being days away. Previously paired scales will continue syncing, but disconnecting them could mean losing automatic weight tracking for good. Smart home gadgets have a habit of outliving the software that makes them smart. A device can work perfectly well for years, only to lose some of its most useful features when its manufacturer decides it’s time to move on. That’s the frustration facing some longtime Fitbit Aria smart scales, which are approaching a deadline that could leave them stuck with little more than ordinary bathroom scales. Starting November 28, 2026 , Google will stop supporting new pairing and re-pairing for the Fitbit Aria and Aria 2 smart scales. The change is tied to Google Health version 5.12, although the app has already moved past that release, with version 5.13 now rolling out .

title: Samsung could end annual Galaxy Watch releases starting in 2027
summary: Fewer hardware launches could mean more time for meaningful upgrades.
body: TL;DR Samsung reportedly plans to skip new Galaxy Watch models in 2027, breaking its annual release tradition. The move to a two-year launch cycle aims to reduce development and marketing costs. Samsung plans to focus on software updates and new health features for existing Galaxy Watches. Not every smartwatch needs a new model every year. Apple demonstrated that when it waited two years between the Watch Ultra 2 and Ultra 3, releasing only a new color in between. And with yearly hardware improvements becoming increasingly modest, there’s a growing debate over whether annual upgrades are still necessary. Samsung could now take things a step further by abandoning yearly Galaxy Watch releases altogether. According to a new report from South Korea’s ETNews , Samsung has decided to skip new Galaxy Watch releases in 2027 and move the lineup to a two-year launch cycle. title: Google explains the 6GB RAM and 10GB storage demands for its new 3D emoji
summary: The numbers make more sense now.
body: TL;DR Google’s new 3D emoji don’t actually require 10GB of storage or consume 6GB of RAM. The 3D font occupies less than 220MB, while the listed hardware requirements are safeguards for automatic downloads. Google hasn’t clarified whether users can opt out of downloading the new emoji. Google’s new Noto 3D emoji were supposed to give Android a fresh look, but their surprisingly demanding hardware requirements have left some users scratching their heads. After all, why should a new set of emoji require 6GB of RAM and 10GB of free storage? While Google’s support page also confirmed that Samsung phones won’t receive the new designs , the hardware requirements sparked another debate, prompting Google to step in with an explanation. The good news? The new emoji don’t actually consume 6GB of RAM or 10GB of storage. According to Google’s Mishaal Rahman (via Reddit ), who verified the details with the emoji design team, the entire 3D font takes up less than 220MB. That’s considerably larger than the roughly 3MB used by the older 2D emoji, but nowhere near 10GB.

title: Molly Meldrum, Australian Music Broadcaster and ‘Countdown’ Host, Dies at 83
summary: "Affectionately dubbed 'The Guru,' Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music," his family said in a statement.
body: Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian broadcaster, journalist and record producer whose weekly television show made stars of international and local acts alike, died Monday (Nov. 23) at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne. He was 83. His family said he died peacefully after a long period of ill health. “Affectionately dubbed ‘The Guru,’ Molly was the heartbeat, the champion and the spirit of Australian music,” they said in a statement. “He shaped not only the sound of a nation but also the dreams of generations who grew up with his voice guiding them.” He is survived by his long-term partner, Yan Wongngam. From 1974 to 1987, Meldrum presented Countdown , the ABC’s Sunday-evening music program, which he co-created with executive producer Michael Shrimpton and producer-director Robbie Weekes. Across 563 episodes, it became appointment viewing for young Australians, and — years before MTV — a showcase that leaned heavily on music video. Swirls and Colors on Jupiter from Juno Explanation: What creates the colors in Jupiter’s clouds? No one is sure. The thick atmosphere of Jupiter is mostly hydrogen and helium , elements which are colorless at the low temperatures of the Jovian cloud tops . Which trace molecules provide the colors remains a topic of research , although small amounts of ammonium hydrosulfide are one leading candidate . What is clear from the featured color-enhanced image — and many similar images — is that lighter clouds are typically higher up than darker ones. Pictured, light clouds swirl around reddish regions toward the lower right, while they appear to cover over some darker domains on the upper right. The protections also block users from taking screenshots inside Signal, but they can be disabled. Signal is calling on Google, Apple, and Microsoft to give app developers better tools to restrict AI access without compromising app functionality. AI assistants are increasingly doing things on our phones that would previously require us to open an app ourselves. Gemini can already order food and book rides using third-party Android apps , and just yesterday, Google started rolling out similar computer-use capabilities on Macs . That’s a question Signal is tackling head-on. The encrypted messaging service announced today that it is introducing protections against AI assistants capturing its content on Android and iOS 27.

title: Samsung’s Auto Blocker won’t switch off during calls in One UI 9.5
summary: Auto Blocker is getting stricter with One UI 9.5 and scammers won't like it.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR With One UI 9.5, users won’t be able to change Auto Blocker settings during a call. This is to thwart scammers trying to get people to disable security features. The feature is already live in the first One UI 9.5 beta on the Galaxy S26. Samsung’s One UI comes with Auto Blocker , which warns you before sideloading APKs and protects your Galaxy phone or tablet from malicious execution over USB or from harmful files received via messaging apps. With One UI 9.5 beta that rolled out to the Galaxy S26 series earlier this week, Auto Blocker appears to be getting additional anti-scam features that prevent hackers from misguiding users during calls. Since Auto Blocker prevents unauthorized apps from being installed, scammers may often attempt to lure users into changing security settings on their devices. Getting users to change these settings makes it easier for scammers to install malicious apps and take over these devices. To prevent this, Samsung is raising the threshold for Auto Blocker and adding measures that prevent users from changing crucial settings while they’re on calls.

title: Google brings computer use to Mac, letting Gemini handle chores without hijacking your screen
summary: Let Gemini do the clicking while you do the working.
body: TL;DR Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac, allowing it to operate desktop apps and websites on your behalf. Gemini works in an isolated background window, leaving your screen and cursor free while you monitor its progress in real time. The feature requires an Apple Silicon Mac and a Google AI Plus, Pro, or Ultra subscription, and is initially available in the US. When Google brought Gemini Spark to the Mac earlier this year, it gave its AI assistant access to local files, allowing it to handle chores like organizing folders and turning documents into spreadsheets. But working with files on your computer and actually operating the apps installed on it are two different things. Google’s latest Gemini update bridges that gap. Just two days after making Gemini Tasks available for free and adding the ability to call businesses, make purchases, and accept requests via text and email, Google is rolling out computer use to the Gemini app for Mac . The feature, which we first learned was in testing in September , lets Gemini click buttons, type, navigate menus, and fill out forms across desktop apps and websites on your behalf.
